checks.note: In the source, 'to my knowledge' qualifies only the testing clause. Marcus states the build claim flatly: 'Strictly speaking Tesla doesn't even build driverless cars.' The proposition puts 'As far as Marcus knows' in front of both parts, which weakens the build claim. It should keep the flat build assertion and hedge only the testing clause. The rationale, limitations, dates and citations are otherwise supported, and 'unresolved' matches the reviews.

The published excerpts are bare pieces: '68% lower' for e1 and '81%' for e2. Both drop the metric and the human-driver comparison. '81%' alone does not even say fewer injury crashes, so readers cannot check the citations. Use the full exact sentences. Also, the '2021–2024 study period' in e1's explanation does not appear in the quoted evidence text. The rationale, limitations (including the Austin 4% figure) and 'supported/conclusive_event' match the evidence and reviews.

The proposition leaves out the 'starved out in the LLM euphoria' funding claim, but the interpretation openly says it is not assessed. The rationale's timeline is right: the Waymo blog (2021) came before the post, and the EMMA paper (v1 2024, v3 2025) and the 56.7M-mile study came later. The excerpts are short but exact and not misleading. 'Unresolved' on the causal axis matches the reviews.

The figures in the rationale (more than 250,000 paid weekly trips across four cities by May 5, 2025; 25.3M driverless miles; fewer liability claims) are supported by e1's context and e2. The Swiss Re study was published on Dec 19, 2024, before the deployment figure, so it fits the early-resolution rule. The limitations disclose Waymo authorship, operator-reported counts, and the dependence on interpretation. The e1 excerpt does not itself contain the trip figures, but it is exact and the locator points to them. 'Supported' matches the reviews.
